key_insight: A scalable unification framework that standardizes and synchronizes diverse 2D/3D autonomous-driving datasets and modalities, enabling them to be combined and used interoperably for large-scale training and evaluation.
problem_solved: Fragmented datasets with heterogeneous formats, sensor rates, sync schemes, and complex dependencies prevent cross-dataset training, benchmarking, and efficient tooling reuse in autonomous driving research.
method: Canonical multi-modal schema + adapters to convert heterogeneous inputs (camera, lidar, ego-state, HD maps, traffic lights, annotations) into a single interoperable format.
Temporal and spatial synchronization modules to align different sensor rates and coordinate frames, preserving timestamps and transforms.
Scalable ingestion, indexing and SDK/wrappers to load, visualize, and train on merged datasets efficiently across environments.
impact: Lowers engineering overhead and boosts reproducibility by making many datasets immediately compatible; enables larger-scale multi-modal model training, cross-dataset benchmarks, and faster iteration for perception and planning research.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: raw datasets -> adapters -> unified schema -> training/benchmarking

Sensor timeline illustrating temporal alignment and resampling across different rates
Sample overlay visualization: camera image with projected lidar points + map/annotation layers
paper_title: 123D: Unifying Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving Data at Scale
paper_authors: Daniel Dauner, Valentin Charraut, Bastian Berle, Tianyu Li, Long Nguyen
